reports.title: Clearway Energy, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Financial Guidance
section: The Company is reiterating its 2026 full-year CAFD guidance range of $430 million to $470 million. The midpoint of the 2026 financial guidance range is based on renewable energy production estimates for the remainder of the year, while the range reflects a distribution of potential outcomes on resource and performance. The guidance range also factors in completing committed growth investments on currently forecasted schedules.

The Company is establishing a 2027 full-year CAFD guidance range of $520 million to $590 million. The midpoint of the 2027 financial guidance range is based on median renewable energy production estimates for the full year, while the range reflects a distribution of potential outcomes on resource and performance in the fiscal year. The guidance range also factors in completing committed growth investments on currently forecasted schedules.

desk.headline: Revenue up 22% to $522m, slight beat; 2026 cash-flow guide reaffirmed, 2027 range of $520–590m set
results: Revenue rose 22% to $522m, just above the $518m expected, as newly bought wind, solar and storage assets added output.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 13% to $435m; cash available for distribution edged up to $173m from $166m.
EPS fell to $0.42 from $1.97 because last year's figure was boosted by losses allocated to outside partners; total net income doubled to $123m.
Renewables output rose 12% and gas fleet availability improved to 93.8%.
The quarterly dividend was raised to $0.4824 a share; liquidity was $1.1bn.

guidance.summary: Clearway kept its 2026 CAFD range of $430–470m (already revised last quarter) and set its first 2027 range of $520–590m. It also set a 2031 target of $3.20–3.40 CAFD per share.

points: The 2027 CAFD midpoint works out to about $2.70 a share; the 2027 dividend target of about $1.98 was kept.
Management said it is on track for the top end or better of its 2030 target and aims for a payout ratio below 70% by 2030.
New long-term contracts for the gas fleet, including up to 500 MW at Walnut Creek, lift earnings visibility.
A planned Wyoming energy complex for data centres, with a letter of intent from a large cloud company, is treated as upside to targets.
Plans include $500m–1bn of new equity through 2029, issued only when it adds to per-share cash flow.
